# Purpose

- To continuously monitor participants' blood glucose levels throughout the study period

# Background

- A Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) is used to assess a person's blood glucose fluctuations over time
- Typically attached to the back of the upper arm, measuring glucose levels every 5 minutes
- Provides more detailed information on glucose levels than a single-point measurement (e.g. finger-prick)

# Scope

- The CGM sensor is applied at Visit 1 (deep phenotyping) after check-in by the DP-Next staff
- Participants wear a subcutaneous CGM sensor on the back of the upper arm, applied a time points during the study: \[DP-NEXT visit-navne, fx V1, V9\]
- Required qualifications/training of personnel performing the examination

# Equipment and Preparation

- 1 new Freestyle Libre Pro iQ sensor (single use only)
- 1 Freestyle Libre Pro iQ reader (**IMPORTANT!** The SAME reader must be used at application and readout)
- Check that the selected reader is charged prior to the visit
- Alcohol wipe for skin disinfection
- Barrier spray and/or kinesiology tape (optional, if adhesion has previously been a problem)

# Safety

- Relevant safety considerations
- Contraindications
- Conditions requiring the examination to be discontinued
- During the first 14 days of \[fase/periode\], the CGM also serves as an additional safety measure

# Deviations, Errors, and Equipment Malfunction

- Expected results: valid readings appear as continuous glucose data at 5-minute intervals within the reader/LibreView system
- **Measurement threshold:** if glucose values exceed 10.0 mmol/l, the participant is contacted by the study site to ensure adherence to the intervention. The participant is also invited to an additional HbA1c measurement. If two separate measurements show HbA1c \> 53, the participant and their general practitioner are informed, and resumption of medical treatment is recommended. **\[TILPAS til DP-NEXT protokol\]**
- Actions to take in case of deviations or technical issues (e.g. sensor falls off, reader malfunction)
- **\[TILPAS\]** Relevant contact persons

# Data

- Data is reported as:
  - Time in Range (3.9–10.0 mmol/l, given in %)
  - Time below Range (\<3.9 mmol/l, given in %)
  - Time above Range (\>10.0 mmol/l, given in %)
  - Coefficient of Variation (measure of glucose fluctuation)
- **Blinding:** Participants do not have access to their own measurements
- **Analysis:** All data from the 14-day wear period is included in analyses, including the first 24 hours. Missing data is not imputed
- **\[TILPAS\]** Where and how data is registered or stored (REDCap-felt/database for DP-NEXT)

# Instructions

- Inform the participant that the sensor is removed after 14 days if it has not already fallen off
- The participant should place the removed sensor in the provided zip-lock bag
- The participant brings the sensor to the next visit

# Procedure

## Application

- Take a new sensor
- Disinfect the application area with an alcohol wipe
- Typically applied to the back of the upper arm - consider asking which side the participant sleeps on
- **Note:** shave the application site if the participant has significant body hair
- If adhesion has previously been an issue, consider barrier spray (applied before sensor placement) and/or kinesiology tape
- Wait until the area is completely dry before applying the sensor
- Open the sensor package and remove the applicator cap. Place the applicator over the sensor, aligning the two markers
- Press the applicator (containing the sensor) firmly against the disinfected area
- Remove the applicator and confirm the tape is securely attached at the sensor's edge
- Turn on the FreeStyle Libre 3 reader by pressing the green button
- Record which reader is used in REDCap (marked 1, 2, or 3)
- Record the sensor ID in REDCap
- Press "Start new sensor" and hold the reader over the sensor
- Wait 2-3 minutes as indicated on screen
- Hold the reader over the sensor again to confirm sensor status; a successful start is confirmed by \[screen indication\]

## Removal and Readout

- Note the participant ID on the sensor
- Turn on the reader and select "Get sensor data." Hold the reader over the sensor until it beeps, then press "Next"
- Connect the reader to a Windows computer using the supplied cable
- Ensure "LibreView Device Drivers" is installed on the computer
- Go to LibreView portal and log in using \[login information\]
- Select "Upload Device"
- Select "Create report linked to patient"
- If this is the participant's first CGM wear: create a new participant profile (see below); otherwise select "Next" and search for the participant by ID
- Creating a participant profile (all data must be pseudonymized):
  - First name: ID followed by underscore, e.g. "1\_"
  - Last name: Visit 1
  - Date of birth:
  - Practice:
  - Email address: leave blank
- Select the participant and choose "Profile" from the left-hand menu
- Select "Download glucose data" at the bottom of the page
- Save the glucose data as a CSV file at: \[DP-NEXT filsti\]
- File naming convention: **\[TILPAS\]** e.g. `dpnext_id_visit_cgm.csv`
- Select "Glucose History" from the left-hand menu
- Select "View report," then "Print/Save PDF"
- **\[TILPAS\]** Save the AGP report as PDF at: \[DP-NEXT filsti\]
- File naming convention: **\[TILPAS\]** e.g. `dpnext_id_visit_cgm.pdf`
- Upload both files (CSV and AGP PDF) to **\[TILPAS - REDCap/system\]**, and archive the sensor
- On the final page of the AGP report, calculate the average glucose from the most recent 4 complete days and enter it into **\[TILPAS - REDCap/system\]** (sum the 4 most recent "Average Glucose" values and divide by 4)
- **\[TILPAS\]** Notify \[relevant contact person\] of participants with newly uploaded CGM data at \[DP-NEXT-specifikt tidspunkt\]

# Documentation and Quality Control

- Confirm sensor ID and reader ID are correctly logged
- Confirm both CSV and AGP PDF files follow the correct naming convention before upload
- Any additional checks and documentation to be carried out during and after the examination

# References

- Battelino et al. 2019 (CGM metrics: TIR, CV)
